chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'O people of Iraq! I have been informed that your women push against men on the road. Are you not ashamed?'

And in another hadith, Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Are you not ashamed nor do you feel ghayrah (protective jealousy/honor) that your women go out to the markets and jostle with the 'uluj (uneducated/faithless men)?'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Title of Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about women's behavior in public markets?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam Ali (AS) addresses the people of Iraq, highlighting the concept of 'ghayrah' (protective honor) as a social responsibility for men to ensure women's modesty in public spaces. He specifically points out two issues: women pushing against men in the streets and mingling closely with 'uluj (often translated as uneducated or faithless men) in the markets. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of 'ghayrah' not just as a personal emotion, but as a communal duty to maintain social decorum and prevent fitnah (temptation).

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Giyas Bin Ibrahim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O people of Al-Iraq! I am informed that your women push men on the road, are you not ashamed?’

And in another Hadeeth, Amir Al Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Are you not feeling ashamed nor feeling a sense of honour that your womenfolk are going out to the markets and ‘الْعُلُوجَ’ (uneducated, faithless) are crowding them?’
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim who has said the following:
“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin once said, ‘O people of Iraq I am informed that your women push men on the road, are you not ashamed?’

In another Hadith it is said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘Are you not ashamed of not exercising vigilance when your women go out in the market and become crowded with al-‘Aluj (uneducated faithless ones)!”’
